column1: Joss/s0|Why only plan for one winter?|I needed somewhere quieter and did not know whether I would settle.|Have you written to your neighbour?|Yes. The cups receive better reports than some people I know.
Joss/s1|Did you ask Tam to stay longer?|Eventually. By then it was clear I was welcome.|What did you put on the hook?|My coat. Such a small thing, and I stopped leaving it packed.

Joss/e0|Was Tam expecting you to stay?|Tam made room without requiring me to decide immediately.|Did you put up anything yourself?|I began treating the place like a home, which was more important than another hook.
Joss/e1|What made you stay?|People I wanted to see again the next morning.|Did you bring enough for the winter?|For one season. The rest I had to work out after admitting I was staying.

Joss/w0|Why did you choose Millwood?|It seemed a place where I could hear myself think and find useful work.|Did the demands follow you here?|Yes. A smaller village is still on the collectors' route.|Did you regret leaving Thornwell?|I missed people. Finding peace here did not mean I disliked everyone there.

Joss/w1|Who would you visit first?|The neighbour keeping my cups. There is a long conversation waiting there.|Would you move back?|I have a home here now. Visiting need not undo that.|Will you bring the cups home?|If they are still considered mine. I may have to negotiate over tea.

Osric/s0|Did your brother act out the adventures?|Whenever he could find something suitable for a sword.|Why did you like the safe way home?|Because an adventure still needs an ending where people return to those who miss them.

Osric/s1|Why did he suspect the cellar?|He had heard a rumour and supplied the rest with enthusiasm.|Did you show him anyway?|Yes. A look at the potatoes was kinder than letting him search for a hidden kingdom all evening.

Osric/e0|Did the heroes remember to eat?|Not often in those books. My brother considered this a serious flaw.|Do you miss the interruptions?|Sometimes. A familiar question can become part of the story.
Osric/e1|Did the traveller accept the answer?|Once he had looked. Potatoes make a fairly unambiguous discovery.|Did he stay for a meal?|Yes. The cellar proved more useful than he first expected.

Osric/w0|What makes a room feel unsafe?|Wondering whether a careless sentence will be repeated to someone with power over you.|Do you still read adventures aloud?|With company that wants them. A shared story can still be a pleasure.|Can a book help people escape the worry?|For a time. Closing it should not mean returning to something worse.

Osric/w1|Would you ever travel yourself?|For a visit, perhaps. I do not need to imitate every hero I read.|What will you read next?|Something with a satisfying return home and fewer royal proclamations.|Will you write about what happened?|I would rather hear the people who were there before attempting that.

Alder/s0|Were the bees reacting to your movements?|To disturbance I could have reduced by working more carefully.|Did slowing down solve everything?|No. It made one avoidable problem smaller. Bees still require attention.

Alder/s1|How do you judge what they need?|The colony, the season and the available stores. A book cannot inspect this year's hive for me.|Do bad winters happen often?|Often enough that I prefer some margin to a perfect prediction.

Alder/e0|Does being calm actually help your work?|It stops me rushing movements and overlooking what the bees are doing.|Have you always been calm around them?|No. The first summer supplied plenty of practice.

Alder/e1|Could you take more in a mild year?|Perhaps, but I will not assume winter will be kind simply because I want more honey.|Is leaving honey a loss?|Only if you ignore the colony that must survive to make any next year.

Alder/w0|Does the levy leave too little for winter?|It can. The demand rarely reflects what the household needs to survive.|Have you explained the comparison?|People here understand it. The collectors are less interested in bees than quantities.|What would sensible collection look like?|Something based on what can actually be spared, with households heard before figures are fixed.

Alder/w1|Will the hives recover this winter?|I can give them better chances. Weather and the colony still matter.|What will you do with extra honey?|Keep enough for the bees and household, then decide what is genuinely surplus.|Why not take advantage of a good year?|I am. A healthy colony next spring is an advantage worth keeping.

Gwyneth/s0|Is Alder pleased with the scarf?|He says so whenever another length appears. He has learned when encouragement is expected.|Could you finish one and start another?|That would be the sensible solution, yes. I am approaching it gradually.

Gwyneth/s1|Did your mother invite many travellers?|Enough that keeping the chair ready became a habit.|Did she ever need the chair herself?|Certainly. Hospitality did not require her to sit cold all evening.
Gwyneth/e0|Would three wraps be too warm?|Possibly. I should let Alder's neck vote before adding another length.|Will you make yourself one next?|A shorter one, if I remember this conversation.

Gwyneth/e1|Do you offer a blanket?|Yes, without making them prove how cold they are.|What if they say they are fine?|I leave the blanket within reach. People can change their minds without an announcement.

Gwyneth/w0|Do you ask what happened on the road?|Only if they want to tell me. A warm chair is not an exchange for information.|Can they rest without talking?|Of course. Sometimes that is exactly why they came.|Have the patrols frightened neighbours too?|Yes. Travelling a familiar road should not require rehearsing answers.

Gwyneth/w1|Will people still come to sit awhile?|I expect so. Tiredness and loneliness have not been abolished.|What would you say to someone still frightened?|That they can stay a little, and need not explain themselves at once.|Does helping tire you too?|Sometimes. I am learning to accept the same kindness back.

Bors/s0|Can different seams leave different dust?|Sometimes the color is distinctive. It is a household observation, not a survey of the mine.|Why did he change chairs?|To see whether I noticed. The dust rather spoiled his experiment.

Bors/s1|Why must the weights match?|Uneven weights pull the threads differently. The weaver needs predictable tension.|How did you learn to make them?|By making, measuring, and listening when a weaver explained what was wrong.

Bors/e0|How do you correct an uneven batch?|I check the weights and sort or remake what does not fit the intended set.|Does a small difference matter?|It can. That is why the weaver should not have to judge by appearance alone.
Bors/e1|Do people use the brush?|More often now they do not have to search for it.|Why not tell them to stop elsewhere?|I tried. Putting the brush where the habit already was proved easier.

Bors/w0|Is your husband often unwell?|The dust affects him enough that I worry. A full cart does not cancel that.|Do the officials count illness as a cost?|Not in the figures they praise in public.|What would you ask them to change?|Listen to the crews about conditions and act before another household has the same worry.

Bors/w1|What should the crews be asked?|What makes the work dangerous and what repairs or changes would actually help.|Would you join that discussion?|If households are invited. We see what follows workers home.|Is producing less an acceptable choice?|If that prevents harm, yes. A larger total is not automatically a better year.

Kiln/s0|What did heating too quickly do?|Cracks and spoiled pieces. Rushing cost more time than it saved.|Do apprentices appreciate seeing mistakes?|Usually. They learn I expect care, not impossible perfection on a first attempt.

Kiln/s1|Can you tell the result before opening?|Some signs help, but the finished pieces still need inspection.|What makes a successful firing?|Sound pieces suited to their purpose. An impressive color does not excuse a crack.
Kiln/e0|Do you check every piece?|Yes. One good bowl does not certify the whole firing.|Does disappointment get easier?|I learn from it more quickly. I do not enjoy wasting work.

Kiln/e1|Do you explain what caused each crack?|Where I know. Guessing confidently would make them poor teaching pieces.|Could broken bowls be mistaken for stock?|I keep the teaching pieces separate. Nobody should buy a fault I already know about.

Kiln/w0|Was the color actually faulty?|It did not match their preference. That was different from the bowls being unsound.|Did you accept the lower offer?|I had little room to bargain with someone speaking for the crown.|Why would they want rejected pieces?|Because they still had a use for them, whatever they called the color.

Kiln/w1|Will you make different colors now?|I can choose work customers genuinely want instead of anticipating royal objections.|Will you still inspect the same way?|Of course. Freedom from a buyer's bullying is not freedom from the craft's requirements.|What makes an honest sale?|A sound piece, its flaws disclosed, and a price both people understand.

Petra/s0|Could rain elsewhere have washed it away?|Yes. I checked the route's reports as well as the dates before accepting the explanation.|Why invent a broken bridge?|It sounded less embarrassing than admitting why the caravan was delayed.

Petra/s1|Do the letters tell you things histories miss?|They tell me what mattered to her on an ordinary afternoon.|Do you reread them often?|When I want her voice rather than just the facts of her life.

Petra/e0|Couldn't someone invent the kindness too?|Certainly. A vivid detail makes a story interesting, not automatically true.|What would you ask next?|Where it happened and how the teller knows. Then compare what can be checked.

Petra/e1|Can you still find a particular date?|Yes. I keep the dates even when the seasons guide the arrangement.|Which letters do you revisit?|The ordinary ones, often. Their small details make her easiest to hear.

Petra/h|Could a price rise have another cause?|Yes. Transport costs or a new charge might do it. That is why the figure starts a question.|Would you compare several towns?|If records survive. A wider pattern helps distinguish a local event from a general one.

Petra/w0|What would a second account change?|It could confirm the first, contradict it, or show what was omitted.|Do official messengers answer questions?|Some. Others treat asking as the offence, which tells me little about the facts.|Are figures harder to falsify than stories?|No. They require sources and checking too.

Petra/w1|Which records need checking first?|The ones affecting what people owe or are owed, while witnesses can still explain them.|Could the new authorities lie too?|Yes. That is why the method must not depend on liking the seal.|How do you preserve a disagreement?|Record both claims and the evidence, rather than silently choosing the convenient one.

Raff/s0|How did the chair help tell the time?|The sun reached it predictably. It was enough to guide the household routine.|What if the day was cloudy?|Then he used other signs. A household habit is not a precise clock.

Raff/s1|Why does evening help?|People are less uncomfortable and have usually had water and food.|Have you ever postponed a conversation too long?|Yes. Waiting for comfort must not become avoiding the subject altogether.
Raff/e0|Did your father explain the trick?|After I had watched it long enough to ask.|Do you use the same routine?|When the sun and the room make it useful.

Raff/e1|What if the matter cannot wait?|Then we find shade and water where possible and speak now.|Do people argue less afterwards?|Sometimes. At least we remove discomfort that has nothing to do with the disagreement.

Raff/w0|Does stopping at noon delay the work?|It changes the schedule. Exhausted workers in dangerous heat are no improvement.|Have officials worked beside you?|Not the ones insisting the timetable matters more than conditions.|What would you ask of them?|Come outside, understand the task, and listen before setting the hours.

Raff/w1|Why are shutters important at noon?|They help keep the strongest sun out of the room.|Should every old custom be kept?|No. Ask what it accomplishes before keeping or discarding it.|What would sensible hours look like?|Work arranged around the heat and the task, with the people doing it consulted.

Suri/s0|Was the bag overloaded?|Partly, and my stitching was poor. Blaming only the load would have taught half the lesson.|Did you repair it on the road?|Enough to finish the journey. I made a stronger replacement afterwards.

Suri/s1|How do you allow room for another layer?|Fit the coat with the kind of clothing the traveller will wear beneath it.|Can a practical coat look good too?|Certainly. It should not look good by making movement or warmth difficult.

Suri/e0|How do you test a strong seam?|With the intended load and movement, not just a neat appearance.|What if a customer finds a fault?|I want to hear about it. A failed seam on the road is worse than criticism at my door.

Suri/e1|Could a pocket spill when you sit?|Yes. Position and fastening matter as well as whether a hand fits.|Do travellers ask for many pockets?|Often. I ask what they plan to carry before adding weight everywhere.

Suri/w0|Why are travellers afraid to stop?|They have been warned about patrols, or delayed by them already.|Can you finish a safe repair quickly?|Sometimes. If not, I say so rather than pretend haste strengthens thread.|Do damaged straps slow them further?|They can. Fear makes them accept repairs they would otherwise question.

Suri/w1|Was the second seam necessary?|Both needed attention. This time I could finish without someone watching the road in alarm.|Did she tell you about the journey?|A little. It was pleasant to discuss ordinary discomforts.|Will business be easier now?|If travellers can stop long enough to have work done properly, yes.

Tavin/s0|Did nobody notice the pack had gone?|We noticed, then stepped around the empty place anyway.|Does your uncle still leave things in doorways?|We remind him before the pack reaches the floor now.

Tavin/s1|How do visitors know they may take it?|I tell them when they arrive. Easy access is less useful if they think it is forbidden.|What if the jug runs empty?|Then I refill it. Hospitality includes checking, not merely putting something down.
Tavin/e0|What tends to get left there?|Bags and things someone intends to move in a moment.|Do guests appreciate a clear entrance?|They rarely mention it. They certainly notice when it is blocked.

Tavin/e1|Do you explain where things are?|Yes. I cannot expect a visitor to recognise every household habit.|What if someone still hesitates?|I offer once, kindly, without making their shyness the subject of the visit.

Tavin/w0|Why did the guards want names?|They thought every arrival ought to be accounted for, even over a drink.|Did you begin asking guests?|No. A thirsty visitor is not automatically a suspect.|Did that cause an argument?|A short one. I kept the subject on water rather than helping them invent a list.

Tavin/w1|Will you change how you welcome people?|The water stays available. I hope the explanation becomes unnecessary.|Are strangers coming more comfortably?|Some seem less guarded. Others still expect questions.|What do you say to someone who is nervous?|Where the water is, and that they can sit for a moment.

Una/s0|What did she send back?|Small useful things, and occasionally something chosen simply to make me laugh.|Did you really want the towels back?|At first. The parcels became a better arrangement than winning the argument.

Una/s1|Will the seeds suit her garden?|I have asked about its conditions. Stubbornness is no substitute for suitable plants.|What if she dislikes gardening?|Then she can say so. A gift should not become an assigned chore.

Una/e0|Was the towel still usable?|Yes, and carefully washed. My sister understands exactly which argument she is prolonging.|Will you send it away again?|Probably around something she did not expect.

Una/e1|Have you included growing instructions?|Simple ones, along with permission to tell me if the experiment fails.|Does she want to try them?|She agreed to a small attempt. I am trying not to turn it into a campaign.

Una/w0|Why hide names on gifts?|Some families fear drawing attention to where their relatives live or whom they know.|How do parcels reach them without a name?|Through someone trusted who already knows the recipient, when that is possible.|Should sending a gift be dangerous?|No. That is why the precautions make me angry.

Una/w1|What will you write to your sister?|Ordinary news, with her name clearly on it. That alone will feel different.|Will you stop being cautious at once?|Probably not. I will still choose a reliable way to send the parcel.|What are you sending this time?|The seeds we discussed, if she still wants to try them.

Vela/s0|Why did your grandmother choose that rule?|She disliked endless picking apart of work that was already useful and beautiful.|Do mistakes ever need fixing?|Certainly. A weak weave is different from a color that merely surprises you.

Vela/s1|How does a turn become a pattern?|My family used a particular shape for each remembered well or bend.|Was your aunt on that journey?|She recognised the family account and places she knew. Her stories gave the pattern more detail.
Vela/e0|Do the knots weaken the rug?|A wrong color does not. A badly made knot would need repairing.|Do you point them out?|Only if somebody asks. The whole rug deserves a look too.

Vela/e1|Would you trust the rug as directions?|Only as a reminder alongside current knowledge. Wells and paths can change.|Who taught you the pattern?|My family, with the stories attached to its turns.

Vela/h|Does every family use the same symbols?|No. You need the maker's explanation before assuming what a shape means.|What if a well is no longer usable?|Then the pattern records an old route. A traveller needs current information.

Vela/w0|Would a renamed road confuse travellers?|It can, especially when older accounts use the familiar name.|Do you still teach the old names?|With their history, so people understand both what was called and what may have changed.|Can a pattern preserve more than names?|It can preserve a family's memory of the journey, if someone keeps telling its story.

Vela/w1|Who would you teach first?|Someone interested enough to ask about the turns, rather than simply copy the border.|Would you let them change it?|Yes, if they distinguish their journey from the one being remembered.|What should stay unchanged?|The honesty of the account. A tradition can grow without pretending the new part was always there.
Wystan/s0|Did you dispute the bill?|Yes. We compared what each of us claimed had been agreed.|Did you buy all sixteen sacks?|I insisted we settle the quantity before any more money changed hands.
Wystan/s1|Do customers return after a fair bargain?|Often. They remember being able to ask questions without a trap.|Is the cheapest price always the fairest?|No. Quality and honest terms matter too.

Wystan/e0|Do you check before paying?|Always. Rereading after payment would teach the lesson less usefully.|What else do you check?|Quantity, condition, price, and whether we mean the same thing by each.
Wystan/e1|What do complaints tell you?|Whether the goods worked as promised, and where I need to explain more clearly.|Have you ever replaced a bad item?|When the fault was mine to put right, yes.

Wystan/w0|What changes in the levies?|Amounts, explanations, sometimes who claims the right to collect them.|Can people refuse the new terms?|Not as they could walk away from an ordinary trader.|Why compare ruling to trading?|Because both involve promises. One should not escape scrutiny simply by having soldiers.

Wystan/w1|Where should agreements be available?|Where the people bound by them can read or have them explained.|What about people who cannot read?|The terms should be explained plainly. Written words are not consent by themselves.|Can written terms still be dishonest?|Yes. They make the agreement inspectable; people must still inspect it.

Rania/s0|Does everyone bring their own chair?|Usually, though we find a place for anyone who arrives without one.|What do you talk about outside?|Work, neighbours, whatever happened that day. The street supplies enough subjects.
Rania/s1|Was Latif embarrassed that you fixed it?|A little. Bringing tea was a very sensible recovery.|Does he repair things better now?|He does. He also still explains them thoroughly.
Rania/e0|What if nobody visits?|Then there is a spare chair and a quieter evening.|Do you invite new neighbours?|Yes. Sitting outside makes a first conversation easier than a formal visit.

Rania/e1|Do you let him finish explaining?|Sometimes I ask which part I should hold while he talks.|Have the chairs lasted?|The properly repaired ones have. Conversation alone remains a poor fastening.

Rania/w0|Do you worry the neighbours will repeat things?|Not all of them. Uncertainty about one listener can quiet a whole group.|Do you avoid his name completely?|We choose our moments. I resent having to choose them.|What would an ordinary evening sound like?|People disagreeing without treating every raised voice as danger.

Rania/w1|What did you disagree about?|What should happen next, and how much change people expected immediately.|Did the argument stay friendly?|Mostly. Freedom to speak does not supply good manners automatically.|Will you meet outside again?|Yes. We did not settle the future of the realm in one evening.

Latif/s0|Did she check your sums?|Every time at first. Fruit was a reward, not proof I could not make mistakes.|Do you still like bruised peaches?|When the sound parts are good. Childhood wages set a lasting preference.

Latif/s1|Can you tell when a story has grown?|Sometimes because I heard its smaller version that morning.|Do you enjoy the polished telling?|If nobody is being deceived about something that matters. A good joke can survive an acknowledged flourish.
Latif/e0|What caused the wrong first count?|Hurrying, chiefly. Mother gave me time to correct it.|Do you count a customer's change twice too?|Yes. An error can inconvenience either of us.

Latif/e1|What if the added detail is harmful?|Then I object. Amusement is not an excuse to put damaging words in someone's mouth.|Have you ever improved a story yourself?|For a joke, yes. I should still make clear when I am embellishing.

Latif/w0|Does separating the charges help?|It shows exactly what was collected instead of blaming every shortage on a poor season.|Do you keep the receipts?|Whenever I can get them, alongside the figures.|Would you show the account to others?|To compare charges fairly, yes, with private details treated carefully.

Latif/w1|Why keep records of an ended levy?|So later claims can be checked against what people actually paid.|Could you use the empty column for something else?|I can begin new pages without erasing the old ones.|Will people care about old figures?|Anyone trying to understand where a household's savings went may care a great deal.

Yara/s0|Which parts suffer first?|Exposed fittings and surfaces. I inspect them instead of waiting for a failure.|Does oiling prevent all damage?|No. It is regular care, not a permanent victory over the weather.

Yara/s1|What brought you back?|The people and the familiar coast. Dry walls did not make the other place home.|Did you ever get used to inland nights?|Somewhat, but I still wanted to hear the sea again.

Yara/e0|How do you remember each week?|I make it part of the household routine instead of waiting for a squeak.|What if the hinge is already damaged?|Then oil alone is not enough. It needs proper inspection and repair.
Yara/e1|Was the inland house quieter?|Quieter in a way I had not learned to ignore.|Would you try living inland again?|For a reason stronger than escaping salt. Every place brings its own work.

Yara/h|How do builders choose the sheltered side?|By understanding the usual weather and the site, not copying a house facing another way.|Can an old house be improved?|Often, though repairs need to respect how it is already built.

Yara/w0|Do you mean the king's taxes?|Taxes and demands presented as protection while the household becomes harder to maintain.|Did his protection help this coast?|Not enough to match what people were asked to give.|What would useful protection look like?|Safe routes and help people could actually rely on, rather than a claim printed over a charge.

Yara/w1|Which promise would you want fulfilled first?|Repairs that keep people safely housed through the weather.|Will you still maintain your own doors?|Of course. Better public decisions do not oil my hinges.|How will you judge the changes?|By what people can see working in daily life.

Doryn/s0|Could the gulls leave for another reason?|Yes. I watch the water and weather too; one sign is not a forecast.|Did your father ever get it wrong?|Certainly. He taught me to pay attention, not to imagine certainty.
Doryn/s1|What needs repairing most often?|The exposed parts. Salt and wet weather are persistent company.|Would you rather live inland?|Some afternoons. Sunrise usually makes me reconsider.
Doryn/e0|Have they stolen your lunch?|Enough of it that I stopped interpreting their interest as friendliness.|Are they afraid of people?|Not when food makes the risk seem worthwhile.
Doryn/e1|Does salt cloud the windows quickly?|Quickly enough to keep the cleaning cloth employed.|Do visitors offer to help?|Rarely. They are very generous with admiration for the view.

Doryn/w0|What does a smiling collector mean?|That an unpleasant demand is about to be presented as reasonable.|Do you trust a blunt one more?|I trust clear terms more than either manner.|Can you prepare for their visits?|Only so far. Weather and collectors can both exceed the margin you kept.

Doryn/w1|Do you really prefer a storm?|I prefer knowing the cause of the trouble. I would be delighted to have neither.|Will you enjoy a quiet day?|Once I have checked what needs mending after the last noisy one.|Has the coast changed already?|People speak more freely. The weather has declined to improve out of courtesy.
Bry/s0|Were you hurt when you slipped?|Only bruised and embarrassed. The soup suffered most.|Did you change anything afterwards?|I started taking that damp step more seriously than my confidence.

Bry/s1|What follows you indoors?|Wet boots, salt, damp air. None of them paid toward the house.|Would a better mat really solve it?|Only part of it. I have learned to give a household purchase a reasonable job.
Bry/e0|Do you laugh about it now?|Usually. Preferably while carrying nothing hot.|Did Coral laugh too?|After checking I was all right. That is the proper order.

Bry/e1|What else keeps the entrance dry?|Drying the step and dealing with wet footwear before walking through the room.|Will you keep living here?|Yes. A damp threshold is a problem to manage, not the whole story of our home.

Bry/w0|Did the patrol apologise?|No. They blamed the stone instead of the shove.|Could the wet step have caused a fall too?|It could. That did not excuse pushing past without care.|Did anyone see what happened?|People nearby did. The patrol was not interested in another account.

Bry/w1|Who would you want the apology from?|The person responsible, if they could acknowledge it without blaming the step again.|Would an apology settle everything?|It would be a beginning. Changed behaviour would matter more.|Will you welcome strangers anyway?|Careful visitors are welcome. I will not give the old patrol every future guest's place.

Coral/s0|Can a boat really see a window lamp?|Only when close enough and conditions allow. It was never a replacement for knowing the harbor.|Why keep the lamp lit, then?|For someone arriving home to see a welcome, as my father did.

Coral/s1|Does the patch affect the sail's strength?|It is soundly sewn. Recognisable should not mean unsafe.|Do you mend other people's sails?|When the job is one I can properly do. Important seams deserve honest limits.
Coral/e0|Does clean glass help the light?|Yes, but I do not imagine one household lamp can guide a boat across the whole sea.|Is tending it comforting?|It is something useful I can do while waiting.

Coral/e1|Could another boat have the same patch?|Of course. He still checks the whole boat before climbing aboard.|Would you use a plain patch if needed?|Certainly. A working sail matters more than a familiar shape.

Coral/w0|Do patrols delay the boats?|They can delay people and cargo at shore, adding another uncertainty to the wait.|How do you find out what happened?|Ask at the harbor when there is news. Worry alone supplies no reliable answer.|What do you do while waiting?|Keep the house ready, mend what needs mending, and try not to invent every possible disaster.

Coral/w1|Will you worry less now?|About the king's men, yes. Weather remains quite capable of keeping me awake.|Has your husband noticed the difference?|He has one fewer set of demands to anticipate when he comes ashore.|Will you keep the window lamp?|Yes. Welcoming someone home is not a habit I want to lose.

Edda/s0|Was the repair worth delaying the table?|Once the storm came, absolutely. Dry shelter made the choice plain.|Did anyone help with the work?|I relied on people who knew roofs better than I did. Saving did not teach me the craft.

Edda/s1|Why not repair the old chair?|It has had repairs. I would like one whose joints no longer need persuading.|What kind of chair do you want?|Sound, comfortable, and suited to the room. Nothing requiring an announcement.

Edda/e0|Do you still worry when rain starts?|Less now, though I check after rough weather.|Have you bought the table yet?|The household needs still determine the order. I will enjoy it when the saving is done.

Edda/e1|Are you still using the old chair?|For now, carefully. I will not keep using it if it becomes unsafe.|Will you discard the rag afterwards?|Perhaps. It has served a surprisingly long apprenticeship in furniture support.

Edda/w0|Did the levy take your repair money?|It made saving slower. A leaking roof did not excuse the demand.|Would you object to every public building?|No. I object to grandeur taking priority while people sleep under leaks.|How many neighbours have similar troubles?|Enough that my roof story is not unusual.

Edda/w1|What should the first building plans address?|Dry, sound homes, particularly for people who cannot manage repairs alone.|Who knows which houses need help?|The residents and people repairing them. Start by asking.|Will you trust the plans immediately?|I will be encouraged when the first leak is actually stopped.
